channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: Natural Harmony · LightBox Photographic Gallery
item.description: LightBox invites photographers worldwide to submit work for Natural Harmony, a show about the land's persistence — a storm overtaking a mountain range, vines reclaiming a forgotten building. The gallery is looking for a modern, expansive reading of "landscape": nature's intersection with humanity, untouched land caught in a moment of change or motion, and enduring yet overlooked corners of the world. The exhibition is juried by Jody Miller, a member of The Guild at LightBox, and runs 10 October – 11 November 2026 at the gallery in Astoria, Oregon, accompanied by live performative work from musicians and writers responding to the images on the walls. Open to any style or medium: traditional, digital and alternative photographic processes are all eligible; fibre-based silver gelatin or archival pigment inkjet for black and white, C-prints accepted. Accepted work must arrive framed and ready to hang, no larger than 20 x 24 inches. Entry is $40 for up to 5 images or $60 for up to 10; artists are notified by 9 September 2026 and accepted work is due 3 October. The gallery retains a 40% commission on sales. — Deadline: September 6, 2026. Fee: $40/5 images, $60/10. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Human Impact Awards 2026 · Wex Photo Video
item.description: Wex Photo Video's annual documentary award, run in partnership with Sony, asks for a 5–10 image series exploring how people shape, affect and respond to the world around them. The brief is deliberately open — community and belonging, identity and representation, climate and land, urban change, protest and social change, care and resilience, ritual, technology, inequality, displacement or simply everyday humanity. Human impact does not have to mean crisis; the judges are looking for thoughtful visual stories with a clear point of view that hold together as a body of work rather than a set of strong singles. Entry is free with no purchase necessary, and images made on any camera, phone or system are welcome. The open Professional Award pays £5,000 for first place, £3,000 for second and £1,000 for third. The Phil Smith Student Photography Award, named in memory of a member of the Wex business team, awards Sony camera and lens kits to its top three students, who enter with a school or university email address. Entries are reviewed by an independent panel of photographers and industry professionals. Photographers retain full copyright; AI-generated imagery and stock photography are disqualified. Open to UK residents aged 18 or over. — Deadline: January 31, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: £5,000.

item.title: Small Wonders 2026 · Maryland Federation of Art
item.description: The 22nd edition of Maryland Federation of Art's annual small-works exhibition, for artists who dream big but work small. Everything must fit under 11 inches in all directions including the frame and display, but there is no limit on creativity or media. MFA exhibitions are blind juried — names and identifying information are hidden from the juror — and this year's selections are made by Abby Daggett, Gallery Director and Marketing Director at Maine Art Hill in Kennebunk, whose background spans commercial galleries and museums in Boston, Venice and Italy. Selected work is shown at MFA's Circle Gallery in Annapolis and its new second location on Maryland Avenue from 25 November to 22 December 2026, with a virtual awards ceremony on 30 November, an opening reception on 3 December and two further Midnight Madness receptions. The juror presents cash awards totalling $1,000. Entry is open to artists residing in any state or territory of the US, Canada or Mexico; up to 6 original works made in the past three years may be entered, and work previously shown at Circle Gallery is not eligible. Artists are notified 29 October and keep 70% of sales (75% for MFA members). Founded in 1963, MFA is a 501(c)(3) non-profit supported by the Maryland State Arts Council. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: $45/2 works ($30 members) + $6.75 each addl. Prize: $1,000 + exhibition.

item.title: Arty Rat Magazine Open Call — September 2026
item.description: Autumn cycle of the Vienna-based independent art journal's rolling open call, inviting artists and photographers worldwide to submit bold contemporary visual work for publication and features. Submitting is free: up to six works go in through the form on the open-call page, or by email. If your work is selected, the publishing options are charged separately — €35 for publication in the magazine, €65 for publication plus an artist page on the Arty Rat website (biography, statement and photographs of works), and €100 for either a curatorial review or a place in the Vienna group exhibition. Selected artists receive a free digital copy of the magazine, photographs of their printed pages and a feature on Arty Rat's Instagram; two artists are chosen for the magazine covers, and one artist is given free participation in Arty Rat's group exhibition at The Names Gallery in Vienna. The call is open to artists worldwide aged 18 or over, and selections are made by Arty Rat's curator Oleksandr Dyvnich. — Deadline: September 1, 2026. Fee: Free (€35–€100 if accepted). Prize: Publication.

item.title: Beecher's 2026 Open Exhibition — Autumn
item.description: Beecher's is a gallery in the market town of Ross-on-Wye, on the edge of the Wye Valley, running a year-round programme of solo and group shows. Its Autumn Open has no set theme and is open to any artist living in the UK, emerging or established, working in painting, drawing, illustration, printmaking, sculpture, mixed media, photography or digital art — all media are eligible except reproductions, film and video. There is a dedicated photography prize, chosen by juror John Bulmer, the photographer who has documented Britain with a photojournalistic eye since the early 1950s and whose exhibition The North opens at Beecher's in January 2027. First prize is a year's representation by the gallery, inclusion in its 2027 group exhibitions, a professional portfolio review and career planning session, and promotion across Beecher's website, newsletter and social channels; further prizes in each category include group exhibitions, business mentoring and marketing, and there is a Visitors' Choice Award decided by votes at the gallery. Judging is anonymous from the submitted images. Around 60 works are selected and hung salon style. Work may not exceed 100cm in any direction or 25kg, must have been completed within 36 months, and must arrive framed and ready to hang. Artists may enter up to six works, and all work must be for sale, with the gallery retaining 50% commission and donating a tenth of that to a partner charity. Selections are announced 6 September, the private view is 17 September and the exhibition opens 18 September; unsold work is collected between 17 and 19 October. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: £20 first entry, £10 each additional (under 22: £12/£6). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Got Rhythm · Grove Gallery
item.description: A themed group show at Grove Gallery on Grove Street in downtown Evanston, run by the Evanston art school Studio 215, asking how artists respond to rhythm, sound and music. The organisers want two-dimensional work that reverberates with the rhythm of life — heartbeat, breath, the cadence of speech — and are open to everything from abstraction to representation, citing Kandinsky's music-driven paintings and centuries of figure painters conveying the movement of dance. Accepted media are painting, drawing, printmaking, photography and textiles; work must hang on the wall, weigh under five pounds and measure no more than 30 inches on the longest side including the frame. Only original, one-of-a-kind works are accepted and open-edition giclée prints are excluded, so a photographer should be entering a print made as the work itself. This is a regional call, limited to artists living in Illinois, Indiana, Wisconsin, Ohio, Iowa, Kentucky or Minnesota. Entries are judged by Melanie P. Brown, a Chicago painter and teaching artist who has performed live painting with local musicians, and Ross Martens and Darren Oberto, both co-owners of Alley Gallery in Evanston — Martens studied Film and Photography at Northwestern and works as an artist, photographer and framer. The exhibition runs across September and October 2026 with an opening reception in early September, and is promoted across the Midwest in Chicago Gallery News, Newcity and elsewhere. All work must be for sale, split 60% to the artist and 40% to the gallery. — Deadline: August 15, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Small Town: Small Works 2026 · Woodstock Arts
item.description: The annual small-format open call at the Reeves House Visual Arts Center, the visual arts wing of Woodstock Arts — a four-acre arts complex north of Atlanta with a performing arts centre, an outdoor music venue, a sculpture garden and a gallery whose shows rotate every eight weeks. Everything in the show is 15 inches or smaller in any direction including the frame, and the call is deliberately hyper-local: entrants must be 18 or over and live within a 15-mile radius of Woodstock, Georgia. Fifteen dollars covers up to five submissions. Photographs and other works on paper must be framed and protected under glass or plexiglass, and hanging hardware is strictly specified — wire, D-rings or a cleat only, no sawtooth hangers, plastic frames or clip frames. Only original work is eligible and pieces previously shown at the Reeves House are not. All work is for sale, split 60% to the artist and 40% to the Reeves House; because the show is hung as a rotating stock, sold pieces go home with the buyer and another work comes out of storage to replace them, so the organisers ask that submissions be similar in size. Notifications go out by 13 October, signed contracts are due 6 November and work is dropped off 2–7 November. The exhibition is on view 13 November 2026 to 2 January 2027, opening with a reception on 13 November from 6 to 8pm. — Deadline: October 6, 2026. Fee: $15 (up to 5 works). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Interdisciplinary Craft + Photography Artist Residency 2027–2028 · Houston Center for Contemporary Craft
item.description: A three-month studio residency in Houston for artists whose practice sits at the intersection of contemporary craft and photography, offered by Houston Center for Contemporary Craft together with Houston Center for Photography. Residents get 24/7 access to a 200-square-foot studio at HCCC, a $1,000 monthly stipend that includes a small housing and materials allowance, and — through HCP — printing credits and full access to HCP's Digital Lab. Residents give a joint artist talk and are included in HCCC's annual In Residence exhibition. Applicants must be able to demonstrate how their work engages both craft and photography; HCCC's programme details list the accepted craft media as wood, glass, metal, fiber and clay, but HCP adds that no particular amount of photographic experience is required, only an interest in showing photo-based work. Residents must work in their studios two days a week during HCCC public hours and open the studio to visitors on Saturdays and one other day. Applications for the 2027–2028 cycle are submitted through the same online application as HCCC's general residency programme, which opens on HCCC's apply page on 1 December 2026 and closes 1 February 2027, with acceptances emailed in late May. Neither organiser has published an entry fee yet — HCP's FAQ answers the fee question with "stay tuned". International applicants must provide proof of eligibility to work in the US. — Deadline: February 1, 2027. Fee: See website. Prize: $1,000/month stipend + exhibition.

item.title: Life Framer — Travel
item.description: The October round of Life Framer's twelve-part monthly award, judged by Michael Yamashita, the American–Japanese photographer whose four decades with National Geographic have taken him across six continents, from the Tibetan Plateau and the Mekong to remote villages and historic trade routes. The brief opens with Susan Sontag — “I haven't been everywhere, but it's on my list” — and asks for the world's landscapes, people and cultures, whether on your doorstep or ten thousand kilometres away. Landscape, travel, portraiture, reportage, street and aerial work are all welcome, from any type of photographer, with images new or drawn from the archive. Analog and digital devices including phones are accepted, and editing, mixed media, collage and compositing are allowed so long as photography is at the heart of the work; AI-generated imagery is not. The monthly first prize is $2,000, part of a $24,000 annual fund shared between the twelve monthly winners, and the first- and second-prize images each month are exhibited in Life Framer's galleries around the world. Entry is tiered: $20 for one image, $30 for three, $40 for six, or $100 for a twelve-month membership allowing up to ten images in every monthly theme. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: $20–$100. Prize: $2,000.

item.title: Atlanta Art Fair 2026 · Atlanta Photography Group
item.description: Atlanta Photography Group is selecting the work for its own booth at the Atlanta Art Fair, which returns to the historic Pullman Yards campus for its third edition on 1–4 October 2026. There is no theme and all photographic genres and processes are welcome. Up to 24 works will be chosen by Andi McKenzie, PhD, Curator of Works on Paper at the Michael C. Carlos Museum; APG's booth at last year's fair was picked by guest curator Melissa Messina as the best curated booth at the fair. Selected works must be no longer than 30 inches on the long side and presented in white frames — no exceptions, and no saw-tooth hangers — and are delivered to the APG Gallery by 25 September. Entry is $70 for up to six works and is open to current APG members only; membership starts at $25 a year for students and $55 for individuals. Notifications go out on or about 28 August 2026. — Deadline: August 21, 2026. Fee: $70 (up to 6 works); APG membership from $25/year. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Human · Dusk Gallery
item.description: Themed exhibition at Dusk Gallery in Santa Fe looking for photographs that get at what it means to be human — not just faces, but the quiet and unguarded moments behind them, the tired eyes at the end of a long day, the burst of laughter that comes out of nowhere, the way we hold each other and hold ourselves together when no one is watching. Portraits and candid work are equally welcome; posed or unposed does not matter, only whether it feels real. Open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers and juried by Dusk founder Holly Hart, who selects 26 images for the gallery walls. The gallery covers professional Luster-paper printing, matting and 24×24 inch black museum-quality framing; artists supply only a high-resolution JPEG (500KB–5MB, 4500px on the longest side). Exhibition runs 4–26 December 2026 with an opening reception on 4 December; prints are archived in the gallery's flat files for six months afterwards, photographers retain all rights, and sales split 50/50. Entry is $40 for 5 images or $45 for up to 10. — Deadline: October 22, 2026. Fee: $40/5 images, $45/10. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Holiday Art Competition 2026 · The Delaplaine Arts Center
item.description: Juried competition and exhibition presented by the Delaplaine Arts Center with the Holiday Committee of Celebrate Frederick, on a secular theme of "The Holidays in Historic Frederick" — winter, downtown, snow and light, built around recognisable Frederick landmarks such as the Carillon, Schifferstadt, the Clustered Spires, Carroll Creek Linear Park and the streets around Market and Patrick. All two-dimensional work in any medium is accepted and photography is named outright alongside painting, drawing, hand-pulled prints, etchings, collage and digital painting; work must be original, unpublished commercially, and able to reproduce in black and white. Judging runs in two rounds — remote review of digital entries, then in-person judging after installation — and accepted work is announced 7 November. The Judges' Choice award is $1,000, with a Barbara Maghan People's Choice certificate voted at the reception and an optional Judges' Special Award. The reception is 2 December 2026, 5:30–7pm, and selected work stays on view in the Community Outreach Gallery 5–27 December. Entrants should note that the Holiday Committee retains exclusive commercial rights to the winning artwork for two years for poster production and five years for other promotional pieces. Accepted work is hand-delivered or shipped to Frederick, framed and wired ready to hang. Entry is $20 per piece. — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: $20 per work. Prize: $1,000 + Exhibition.

item.title: Nostalgia · New Hampshire Art Association
item.description: Member show at the New Hampshire Art Association's Portsmouth gallery built around memory and the act of looking back — personal histories, shared experiences, places once known, cherished objects, cultural touchstones, and moments that continue to resonate as they pass on. NHAA welcomes artwork in any medium and names photography outright in its list alongside painting, drawing, printmaking, mixed media, sculpture, installation, fibre arts and digital work, provided it engages with the theme. This is not a juried show: all member entries are accepted, though the association notes it may have to limit accepted works by size if response outstrips available wall space. Entry is $12 for the first piece and $10 for a second, and NHAA membership is required — artists can join when applying. The exhibition runs 2–27 September 2026 at 136 State Street with an opening reception on 4 September, 5–8pm; work is dropped off 30–31 August and collected 27–28 September. Sales split 60/40 in the artist's favour. — Deadline: August 25, 2026. Fee: $12–$22. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Reflections 180 Years of Manchester NH · Mosaic Art Collective
item.description: Manchester, New Hampshire has spent 180 years becoming itself, and Mosaic Art Collective is asking artists to look closely at it — the mills along the Merrimack, the neighbourhoods, industries and people who have reshaped the city again and again, and the city as it exists today. Work can be documentary or interpretive as long as it speaks to reflection on Manchester's history and present; all media are welcome except reproductions and AI-generated work. This is a lightly juried call. The exhibition runs 12 September – 26 October 2026 at Mosaic Studios, 66 Hanover Street, with an opening reception on 12 September, 5–7pm; acceptance notices go out 24 August and accepted work is dropped off 26–28 August. Entry is $10 for up to four works and sales split 75/25 in the artist's favour. Work must arrive ready to hang with d-rings and picture wire, or a $5 wiring fee applies at drop-off. — Deadline: August 21, 2026. Fee: $10. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Full Circle — New Beginnings 2026 · Mosaic Art Collective
item.description: Mosaic Art Collective marks its fourth anniversary and its move to a new street-level gallery in Manchester, New Hampshire with a show about cycles: the seasons we move through, the relationships that anchor us, the personal transformations that bring us back to ourselves in new form. A return to an old practice, a fresh start after loss, the quiet repetition of daily rituals — the collective wants to see how artists interpret what it means to come full circle. All media are welcome except reproductions and AI-generated work. Entry is $10 for the first work and $10 for each additional, up to four. The exhibition runs 7–28 September 2026 at the collective's gallery on Chestnut Street with an opening reception on 12 September, 5–7pm, and acceptance notices on 30 August. Sales split 75/25 in the artist's favour, and work must arrive ready to hang with d-rings and picture wire or a $5 wiring fee applies at drop-off. — Deadline: August 28, 2026. Fee: $10–$40. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 78th Regional Exhibition · Arnot Art Museum
item.description: For over seventy-five years the Arnot Art Museum's Regional Exhibition has gathered artists from across the Northeast and Eastern Canada into a museum setting, and the 78th edition is open now. Photography is named outright in the museum's own media list alongside painting and drawing, sculpture, graphics, clay, textiles, jewelry, wood and metal work, and mixed media. The Museum keeps a primary focus on representational art but explicitly welcomes non-objective work for the Regionals, so the door is open to conceptual and abstract lens-based practice too. Up to $10,000 in cash awards is distributed among the juror selections, and selected artists receive two complimentary tickets to the Gala Reception and Awards Ceremony on 19 December. Work is shown in the Museum's West Wing Galleries from 29 September to 19 December 2026. Entry is open to artists 18 and over living in Connecticut, Delaware, Maine, Massachusetts, New Hampshire, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania, Rhode Island or Vermont, or in Ontario, Canada; work must be no more than five years old and not previously shown at the Museum. Maximum two entries per artist, nothing over 96 inches or 150 pounds, and a 40% commission applies to sales made during the exhibition. — Deadline: August 17, 2026. Fee: $30–$50. Prize: $10,000 + exhibition.

item.title: We Are the Ones · Willow Street Gallery
item.description: Willow Street Gallery, the exhibition project of DC Arts Studios in the Takoma neighbourhood, is looking for work about community — what it means to hold and be held by other people, and to build something better together. The theme takes its title from the closing line of June Jordan's Poem for South African Women, and the gallery is explicit that it is a starting point rather than a literal brief: the call frames healing as a communal endeavour and resilience as something rooted in giving of yourself and receiving the care of others. Photography is named directly in the accepted media, alongside painting, drawing, mixed media and textile art; the gallery can take 2D work in any physical medium but cannot accommodate video or other digital media this round. Open to artists 18 and over living and working in the greater Washington DC region — DC, Maryland and Virginia. Two cash prizes are awarded, $200 for best in show and $100 for the runner-up, and the show runs 12 September to 3 October 2026, with an opening reception on 12 September and a closing reception on 2 October. DC Arts Studios has served the DMV since 1979 and keeps its gallery commission at 20% rather than the usual half. — Deadline: August 16, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: $200 / $100 + exhibition.

item.title: Reel Pride 2026 Art Show
item.description: The Reel Pride Art Show is the gallery arm of Winnipeg's Reel Pride International Film Festival — a space for 2SLGBTQI+ artists to show work alongside the festival at The Gas Station Arts Centre. The organisers welcome work in all forms and mediums and are open about what they are after: personal expression, a statement, or a celebration, and the many ways queer and Two-Spirit people experience and build community. There is no entry fee. If work sells the artist keeps the full sale price — the festival takes no commission — and artists retain full copyright, with images used only to promote Reel Pride and its events. Submissions run entirely through the call site, and accepted work is dropped off in Winnipeg during the week of 7–11 September. The show runs 15 to 20 September 2026 alongside the festival. — Deadline: September 4, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Artist-in-Residence Program: Winter and Spring 2027 · Mosesian Center for the Arts
item.description: The Mosesian Center for the Arts in Watertown runs its second Artist-in-Residence Program with a straightforward proposition: free studio space and professional development support, no fee to participate beyond a refundable key deposit. Photography is named directly in the list of eligible visual-art disciplines, alongside painting, sculpture, printmaking and mixed media, and the programme also takes performing, literary, interdisciplinary and socially engaged artists. Residents get a private or shared 11 by 22 foot studio with 24-hour access for three months, a welcome reception, and $45 an hour (minimum 1.5 hours) for any workshops or classes they teach during the residency. Two to three General Artist Residencies are offered free of charge. One Ignite Artist Fellowship is selected from this cycle, carrying the same free studio space and professional development support for an emerging artist from the global majority or a historically marginalised community, plus a $1,000 stipend towards materials, transport or project costs. The programme is aimed at emerging and mid-career local and regional artists looking for time and space to experiment. Housing, per diem and materials are not otherwise included, and residents are expected to share their work through at least one public-facing event — an open studio, artist talk, workshop or performance. Winter residency runs January to March 2027, spring runs April to June, and selected artists are announced 15 October 2026. Applications ask for eight images or files, a CV, an artist statement and a short bio. — Deadline: September 8, 2026. Fee: $20. Prize: Residency.

item.title: The New Masters 4: Women Artists of Northeast Ohio · Florence O'Donnell Wasmer Gallery
item.description: The Wasmer Gallery on the Ursuline College campus hosts the fourth edition of its juried exhibition for women artists living and working in Northeast Ohio. The gallery enumerates photography explicitly among the accepted media — traditional, digital and computer-enhanced — alongside painting, works on paper, mixed media, sculpture, glass, fiber and jewelry, and giclée reproductions are barred except for signed and numbered limited editions or photography. Open only to women artists 18 and over, emerging and professional, currently residing in the eighteen counties of Northeast Ohio: Ashland, Ashtabula, Columbiana, Cuyahoga, Erie, Geauga, Huron, Lake, Lorain, Mahoning, Medina, Portage, Richland, Stark, Summit, Trumbull, Tuscarawas and Wayne. The guaranteed minimum prize pool is $500, rising with the number of entries, and is split across Best in Show, an Award of Excellence for first prize and an Award of Distinction for second; final amounts are announced on 12 September with acceptance notifications, and cheques are issued by Ursuline College. Up to three works per artist at $10 each, capped at $30. Work must be original, made in the last five years, not made under instruction in a class or workshop, and not previously shown at the Wasmer Gallery. 2D work including mat and frame must be no larger than 30 by 40 inches. — Deadline: September 6, 2026. Fee: $10 per work. Prize: Cash awards + Exhibition.

item.title: Abbott Watts Photography Residency — Winter 2027 · Monson Arts
item.description: Monson Arts' dedicated photography residency, reserved within its general open call, gives one photographer per session access to the private studio and darkroom of Todd Watts in Blanchard, Maine — adjacent to the former home of Berenice Abbott. The darkroom takes silver gelatin prints up to 40×50 inches from negatives between 35mm and 8×10 and supports other analog and alternative processes; the digital side has PC workstations with 34-inch monitors and Adobe Creative Cloud, a 44-inch Epson printer, scanners, trimmers and a 48×96-inch dry-mount press. Residents supply their own film, paper, chemistry and ink. The winter 2027 open call runs August 1 to September 15, 2026 and covers three sessions, of which the four-week January 25 – February 18 session is the one that carries the Abbott Watts placement. Residents receive a private bedroom in shared housing in Monson, all meals, a $500 stipend for the four-week session, and join a cohort of five visual artists and five writers. A car is needed for the eight-minute drive to the Blanchard studio; cell service is very limited in both locations. Applications go through SlideRoom and are open to artists at any career stage, US and non-US citizens with working knowledge of English, who are not currently enrolled in a BFA or MFA program. — Deadline: September 15, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: Residency + stipend.

item.title: Enigmatic Encounters: The Veil Grows Thin · Create Appalachia
item.description: Create Appalachia's autumn show at the Kingsport Center for Art & Technology asks what emerges when the boundary between worlds turns fragile. Drawing on folklore, spirits, dreams, unseen forces and the liminal places between the known and the unknown, the call seeks work that is eerie, ethereal or enchanted — ghostly encounters, ancient legends, supernatural landscapes, forgotten memories, or personal readings of the unseen. Photography is named in the accepted media alongside painting, illustration, sculpture, pottery, mixed media, installation, short film, video, animation, game art, digital illustration, graphic design, 3D print and fibre work. This is a physical gallery show, not an online display: digitally made work is printed and hung, and moving image runs on monitors with a two-minute cap. AI artwork is not accepted. The entry fee covers up to three submissions, with each additional set of one to three files charged again. Selected artists are notified three days after the deadline; work is dropped off in person or shipped with prepaid return labels, and the gallery takes 30% commission on sales. The exhibition opens August 28 with a reception on September 3 and runs to October 30, 2026. — Deadline: August 12, 2026. Fee: $30 (up to 3 works). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Seasons of Change · Mountain Artists Guild
item.description: The Mountain Artists Guild's autumn juried show in Prescott, Arizona takes transformation as its subject — shifting seasons and weather, migration and seasonal wildlife, personal growth, new beginnings and endings, healing and resilience, time and nostalgia, and abstract readings of movement and change. Photography is one of the four judged categories in its own right ("all types of photography mediums"), alongside original paintings, three-dimensional objects and handcrafted jewellery. The call is open to members and non-members alike, with Arizona artists particularly encouraged; up to five works may be entered, the first three covered by the base fee and each further work charged separately. Entries are juried for the gallery show and then judged again in the gallery, with an awards ceremony and reception on September 25. Reproductions of original paintings, giclées and printed merchandise such as tote bags are excluded, as are nudes and work unsuitable for family viewing; canvas or frame size must be at least 154 square inches and no more than 1,728. All artwork must be for sale and delivered in person — no shipping — with gallery intake on August 31. The Guild takes 25% commission from members and 40% from non-members. The exhibition runs September 2 to October 24, 2026, and accepted work also stays in the online Web Gallery for three months. — Deadline: August 22, 2026. Fee: $30 members / $45 non-members (up to 3 works). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: A Charles River Journey · Dedham Art Association
item.description: Eighty artists, eighty miles: the Dedham Art Association and the Wellesley Society of Artists, working with the Charles River Watershed Association, are assembling an exhibition that follows the Charles River along its full course from Hopkinton to Boston. Artists are asked for visual impressions of the river — its meandering natural landscapes, the communities it connects, and its role as both a recreational and an ecological resource — with the flora, fauna, people and places reimagined as a record of the environmental and social narratives of the moment. Photography is named in the accepted media alongside painting, drawing, mixed media and collage, and printmaking; each artist submits one original two-dimensional work. Eighty works will be juried in and are eligible for over $2,500 in cash awards. The call is open to artists living in New England, emerging and established, as well as students enrolled at New England universities. Selected work is announced December 1, 2026, delivered in January, and shown at the Dorothy and Charles Mosesian Center for the Arts in Watertown, Massachusetts from January 22 to March 12, 2027, with an opening reception on January 28. — Deadline: November 1, 2026. Fee: $30–$40. Prize: Cash awards + Exhibition.

item.title: When Light Gathers · Pierro Gallery
item.description: The Pierro Gallery of South Orange opens a group exhibition bringing together local and regional artists with connections to Jewish culture and community. Opening in December during Hanukkah, the show is timed to a season associated with light, gathering and reflection, and it is explicitly not a religious brief: the gallery states that artists are not expected to engage with religious or cultural themes in their work, and that the exhibition exists to let many voices be seen together. Emerging and established artists are both welcome, and up to three works may be submitted with title, medium, dimensions, year and price; a short artist statement and bio are requested only if the work is selected. Founded in 1994 and run by the South Orange Department of Recreation and Cultural Affairs, Pierro is a non-commercial municipal gallery that charges no submission fee and takes no commission on sales, inviting a voluntary donation instead. The gallery accepts photography alongside painting, sculpture and mixed media, and works needing glass or Plexiglass must meet its standard framing guidelines. Artists are notified the week of 12 October 2026, and the exhibition opens 3 December 2026 at the Baird Community Center, 5 Mead Street. — Deadline: September 24, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: The Wellspring of 1000 Eyes · The Art Department, Paisley
item.description: The Art Department, Paisley marks the first year in its new permanent home — a former Argos store on Causeyside Street — with an open call built on the phrase "Keep your Eye on Paisley", which the organiser attributes to Benjamin Disraeli, and on Argos Panoptes, the hundred-eyed giant of Greek myth set to watch and never sleep. Artists are invited to respond to Vintage Paisley (any photograph or artwork of the town's past or present) and to the broader themes of Power & Guardianship, The All-Seeing Eye, The Eyes of the Truth, The Third Eye, The Public Eye and Private Eye. Photography is named among the media the exhibition will feature, and the entry guidance is explicit that works may be of any medium or genre. There is no entry fee and no hanging fee — the project is supported by Renfrewshire Council's Culture, Heritage & Events Fund — and up to six works may be submitted per artist, all through the online form. Work is graded by a selection panel using an average-score system; artists are notified on 8 November 2026, hand-in runs 16–30 November, and the exhibition opens 1 December 2026 and closes 30 January 2027. Most work is expected to be for sale, with a 30% commission plus VAT on the commission element supporting the charity, and remittance by 31 March 2027. — Deadline: October 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Aggregate IV: Rock On! · School of Art Collection and Galleries, Kent State University
item.description: The School of Art Collection and Galleries at Kent State University opens its fourth Aggregate — a national juried exhibition whose brief is deliberately wide: open to all artists living in the United States working in any medium, gathering the range of what is being made across the country. Entrants may submit up to three pieces for a flat $10 fee, one JPEG per work, and only works submitted online and selected by the judges will be shown. The exhibition runs 6 November 2026 to 9 January 2027 at the KSU Downtown Gallery, 141 East Main Street in downtown Kent, Ohio, with an opening reception on 6 November from 5 to 7 p.m. A $500 first prize and a $300 runner-up prize are awarded. Accepted work must reach the gallery no later than 28 October 2026, must stay up for the run of the show, and cannot be substituted; hanging work needs a professional hanging device (no tape or loosely attached wire), and every piece must be labelled with the artist's name, title, medium, dimensions and price or insurance value. The galleries programme comprises eight exhibition spaces on the Kent campus and in downtown Kent, showing local, regional, national and international artists with new exhibitions every four to six weeks, supported by the Ohio Arts Council. — Deadline: October 4, 2026. Fee: $10. Prize: $500 / $300 + Exhibition.

item.title: Beauty That Remains · Kingdom Bound Ministries
item.description: Kingdom Bound Ministries and Project Lab are gathering work for a one-day community art exhibition in Buffalo's Sheridan Parkside neighbourhood, built around faith, restoration and what endures through hardship. The call is for work that speaks to rebuilding — restoration, redemption, peace, resilience, compassion, healing and the beauty that survives difficult seasons — and especially to community: the ways people come together to support one another and carry hope forward. Work may be symbolic, abstract, deeply personal or narrative-driven. Accepted media are listed explicitly and include photography alongside painting, drawing, sculpture, mixed media, digital art, printmaking and textile/fibre work; AI-generated art is not accepted. The exhibition is a fundraiser tied to the conversion of a long-closed school building into the Sheridan Parkside Life Center, a space for connection, care and creativity, and proceeds also support the centre's literacy initiatives for local children. Artists may submit one to ten images for a $25 fee; selected work is shown on 19 September 2026 from 11am to 4pm at 169 Sheridan Parkside Drive, Tonawanda, New York, with a raffle of donated pieces running through the day and artists able to sell their work on a 60/40 split. Notification is 26 August 2026. — Deadline: August 17, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Zari Art Prize 2026 · Zari Gallery
item.description: The Zari Art Prize returns for 2026 from Zari Gallery, a Fitzrovia gallery in London's West End founded in 2016 to show new and established artists united by mixed cultural heritage. The prize is awarded across three categories — painting, sculpture and photography — from a £4,000 prize pool, with Photography taking £550 and Photography Runner-up £350 alongside a £1,000 Best in Show and a £300 People's Choice. There is no set theme. Artists worldwide may submit up to ten works; entry is £20 for a single work, rising on a sliding scale to £87.50 for ten. Judges select an online shortlist between 23 and 31 August, a public vote opens 2 September, and the shortlist is announced 9 September, with shortlisted work delivered 11–17 September for the gallery exhibition in central London. Photographs must arrive framed and fitted with hanging hardware; images are submitted as JPEGs under 10 MB, ideally 300 dpi and at least 1600 pixels wide. Work is offered for sale to the gallery's collector audience. — Deadline: August 22, 2026. Fee: £20 (1 entry) – £87.50 (10 entries). Prize: £1,000 Best in Show + Exhibition.

item.title: Weathered & Fired: Barnstormers and Atmospheric Fired Ceramics · Artspiration Frederick
item.description: Artspiration Frederick invites original work inspired by barns, farms, rural landscapes and the passage of time in Frederick County, Maryland — from weathered wood and rusted metal to atmospheric fired ceramics that embrace the elements. All media are accepted and photography is named explicitly alongside 2D, 3D, ceramics, sculpture and mixed media. Artists may submit up to three pieces and up to three may be selected; all work must be original, exhibition-ready and for sale, with 2D work properly framed and wired (no sawtooth hangers). The exhibition runs 2 October to 1 November 2026 with an artists' reception on 10 October, in a gallery that is free to enter, open to the public and wheelchair accessible. Accepted work is dropped off 29–30 September, or shipped to arrive by 29 September at the artist's cost with a prepaid return label. Jurors are potter Tony Clennell, a Royal Canadian Academy of Arts member with an MFA from Utah State who has taught across four continents, and Kimberly Yourick, founder of Lockhouse Gallery in Brunswick, Maryland and an oil painter specialising in plein air landscapes. Notification is emailed the week of 21 September. — Deadline: September 11, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: New/Now: Pondering Change · South Haven Center for the Arts
item.description: National juried exhibition at the South Haven Center for the Arts on Michigan's Lake Michigan shore, built around change as the one constant of human experience — joyous, tragic, sudden or gradual, and above all the way we react to it. Artists are asked to muse on a deviation in their life, work or world and make a piece that reflects their response to a change experienced, anticipated or initiated, with a brief note on how that change informed the work. Open to artists residing in the United States and the Tribal Nations that share these geographies, in any visual medium; work must be original and completed within the last five years, with a maximum of two entries. Two-dimensional work is capped at 72 by 55 inches, three-dimensional work must fit through a standard doorway and stay under 50 pounds, and no installations or ceiling-hung work are accepted. Juried by David Baker, artist and professor emeritus at Southwestern Michigan College and a longtime teacher at Ox-Bow. Awards are $500 for first place and $250 for second; the show runs 26 September to 7 November 2026 with an opening reception on 25 September. Entry is $25 for up to two works, reduced to $10 for students and artists facing unforeseen hardship. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: $25 (2 works), $10 reduced. Prize: $500 / $250.

item.title: In Flux · Oceanside Museum of Art
item.description: Juried exhibition for members of the Oceanside Museum of Art's Artist Alliance, staged off-site at Covet Art Gallery in the South Oceanside district north of San Diego. The show is loosely rather than strictly themed: artists are invited to read the title however they like, with the call pointing toward physical, emotional or environmental change — work that expresses movement, transformation or uncertainty, whether through shifting materials or shifting ideas. Selection is by Laurie King, who founded Covet Art Gallery in December 2023, and is made with an eye to which pieces build the strongest show in combination. Up to 20 works may be entered and a maximum of two per artist will be selected. Photography is explicitly accepted alongside limited-edition prints in traditional printmaking media and limited-edition digital prints; other reproductions of original works are not. Two-dimensional work is capped at 84 by 84 inches and smaller pieces have a better chance given space limits. Eligibility requires current OMA membership at any level with the $25-per-person Artist Alliance add-on, and entry scholarships are available on request. Entry is $25 for the first submission and $10 for each after; the exhibition runs 3–29 October 2026 with a public reception on 3 October. — Deadline: August 10, 2026. Fee: $25 + $10 each additional. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Virtual 46th Annual Juried Photographic Exhibition · Marie Selby Botanical Gardens
item.description: Marie Selby Botanical Gardens in Sarasota has run this juried photography exhibition for forty-six years, and the 2026 edition is presented online, with entries submitted digitally and every accepted photograph shown in a virtual gallery. Five categories are open: Living Art, Make a Splash, Plant Portraits, The Birds and the Bees, and Black + White. The headline award is the Richard and Ellen Sandor Photography Prize, $5,000 annually for the best artistic representation of an orchid species from any category, judged by a panel on artistic merit, creativity and visual impact. Images must be original, owned by the entrant, shot within the past year at either of the Gardens' two campuses — Downtown Sarasota or Historic Spanish Point — and not previously published for compensation; volunteers may not enter work made during service. Files may carry no watermarks, words, graphics or clearly identifiable people, and each photographer may enter a maximum of three. Entry is $45 for the first image and $15 for each additional, dropping to $30 and $10 for Selby Gardens members. The submission window is short: 3 to 10 August 2026, closing at 5pm on the tenth. Awards are announced online on 27 August and the exhibition runs through 30 September. — Deadline: August 10, 2026. Fee: $45 first entry, $15 each additional ($30/$10 members). Prize: $5,000.

item.title: Freedom's Journey · New England Black Artists Collective
item.description: Juried exhibition marking the 200th anniversary of Freedom's Journal — America's first Black-owned and Black-operated newspaper, founded in New York in 1827 by Samuel E. Cornish and John B. Russwurm in response to the exclusion and misrepresentation of Black Americans in the mainstream press. The New England Black Artists Collective invites submissions in any medium, and explicitly names photographers alongside sculptors, mixed-media and interdisciplinary artists; the call particularly welcomes creatives with lived experience as members of the African diaspora. Artists are asked what "Freedom's Journey" meant to the paper's original readers, and what it means now — what freedom looks like personally, to a family, to a community, who has led the journey towards it, and what has deferred it. Up to five works may be submitted with a 150–250 word artist statement plus a statement tying the work to the theme; new and existing work are both eligible. Selected work is shown at the Krikorian Gallery at the Worcester Center for Crafts in Worcester, Massachusetts. Three jurors read the entries: Toby Sisson, Associate Professor and Director of the Visual Arts Program at Clark University; Deborah Hall, founder and director of the Worcester Black History Project; and Candace Casey, Gallery Director of the Krikorian Gallery. They name a best of show, which carries a $500 cash prize, and two honorable mentions. Wall pieces must arrive wired and ready to hang (no alligator hooks); textiles may run up to 88 by 90 inches and all other work up to 65 by 60 inches. Artists are notified by 3 January 2027 and jury results are announced by 6 January; work must be in house — delivered or mailed with return postage — by 16 January, and the exhibition runs 1–28 February 2027. — Deadline: December 1, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: $500 Best of Show + Group exhibition.

item.title: Fall into Art 2026 · San Marcos Art League
item.description: The San Marcos Art League's autumn open show at the San Marcos Art Center, asking for work that carries the colours and traditions of the season — from pleasant autumnal memory to the new adventures that arrive as the year turns. Open to all artists across every medium, with photographs, fine art prints and digital art named explicitly alongside sculpture, textiles and pottery. Each artist may enter one original work completed in the last 24 months and not previously shown at the Art Center Gallery. Two-dimensional work must be framed or gallery-wrapped with no visible staples, wired for the gallery's hanging system, and no larger than 36 by 68 inches including the frame; three-dimensional work is considered on size and stability. All work must be hand-delivered — the Art Center does not accept shipments — with intake on 30 August, a public reception on 11 September and pickup 1–2 October. Work must be for sale at a price fixed at entry, and the Art League retains a 20% commission. Entry is $10 for Art League members with the code sent to them by email, and $20 otherwise; submissions close 28 August at 5pm or when the show fills. — Deadline: August 28, 2026. Fee: $20 ($10 members). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Fotosalongen 2027 · Hasselblad Foundation
item.description: Sweden's largest photography salon returns for its second edition at the Hasselblad Center in Gothenburg, and the open call is deliberately wide: amateur and professional photographers working across every genre are invited to submit, with no set theme. The foundation welcomes documentary photography and photojournalism alongside nature, family, street, science, politics and art photography, and says the salon is built to create unexpected encounters between established artists, emerging talents and photographers whose work has never been shown publicly. The jury looks for compelling images and photographic narratives with depth, originality and a diversity of expression, so that the selected works together offer a broad snapshot of photography today. Submissions are still photography only — no video — as up to five single images, or an installation without electronic equipment; one project per person or group, and groups may apply jointly. Entry is free. Selected photographers exhibit at the Hasselblad Center, receive compensation of SEK 3,200, appear in the exhibition catalogue and may sell work; participants cover transport of works to and from the Center. The jury is chaired by the foundation's chief curator Dragana Vujanović Östlind and includes Alexandra Ellis of the Sune Jonsson Centre for Documentary Photography at Västerbottens museum, film director Tarik Saleh and photographer Elisabeth Toll. Applications run from 1 August to 18 October 2026 via Picter; the exhibition itself runs 23 April to 26 September 2027, in a venue that draws around 70,000 visitors. Open to anyone who turns 18 during the application year or is older, and who is either a Swedish citizen or has a residential address in Sweden. — Deadline: October 18, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: SEK 3,200 + Exhibition.

item.title: The Cat Show · Blue Sky Gallery
item.description: The twelfth and final show in Blue Sky's year of 50th-anniversary online exhibitions, and a direct answer to the gallery's 1976 group show The Dog Show. Exhibitions Director C. Meier — a self-described cat enthusiast — juries the call, looking for the most clever, curious and chaotic feline companions: humorous snapshots and thoughtful fine art are equally welcome, and every photographic approach is in scope. The pitch is that photographers and cats have at least one thing in common, a love of light, whether that means a favourite sun spot or an iconic pose. Entry is free and Blue Sky membership is not required. Artists may submit up to three images as JPGs no larger than 1500 pixels on the longest side, named lastname_firstname_title.jpg and accompanied by title and year; submissions are accepted only through the gallery's Google Form. Accepted work is shown online only and is not for sale. Images that violate Blue Sky's anti-discrimination policy or are otherwise deemed offensive will be disqualified, as will submissions that ignore the file requirements. Accepted artists are notified by email; because of the volume of entries, unsuccessful submissions do not receive a reply. The deadline is Friday 28 August 2026 at 11:59pm Pacific, and the exhibition launches Friday 25 September 2026. — Deadline: August 28, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: Overshoot · DOTLOGIC
item.description: The first open call from DOTLOGIC, the Trieste social cooperative behind URBAN Photo Awards, Exhibit Around, dotART and Trieste Photo Days, asking photographers worldwide for their own account of climate change. The title refers to the crossing of the 1.5°C threshold: 2024 was the first full year above it, and the call takes that as the beginning of what science calls an overshoot, where every fraction of a degree brings consequences that are more severe and less reversible. Submissions can approach the theme through landscapes in transformation — coasts, mountains, farmland, cities — or through people: those who work, adapt or resist in the face of climate effects, the everyday gestures a changing climate transforms, and more conceptual readings of the distance between what the numbers say and what bodies feel. Any genre is welcome, from reportage and documentary to street, landscape and fine art, but only single photographs are admitted; no projects or portfolios. AI-generated or AI-manipulated images are strictly prohibited, as are watermarks and signatures. Files must be JPG, RGB/sRGB, at least 2000 pixels on the short side and under 10MB. Twenty selected photographs are exhibited at Magazzino 26 in Porto Vecchio, Trieste from 23 October to 8 November 2026 alongside work by Mark Power and Christopher Morris, the international guest artists of Trieste Photo Days 2026, with full production — printing and setup — covered by the organisers. Selected authors are published in the official Magazzino 26 catalogue, receive a limited-edition commemorative coin, and may be considered for future Exhibit Around exhibitions. Authors keep moral and intellectual property rights; the organisers take non-exclusive promotional rights with author credit. The entry fee is €20, and the number of photographs you may submit depends on your Exhibit Around membership tier, from one image for non-members up to twenty-five at the top level. The call runs 1 to 31 August 2026 and responds to Goal 13 of the UN 2030 Agenda. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: €20. Prize: Exhibition + Catalogue.

item.title: 6 by Exhibit 2026 · Cape Fear Studios
item.description: A small-works call with one governing rule: one dimension of each piece must measure six inches, before framing. Cape Fear Studios in downtown Fayetteville opens it to visual artists in any medium, photography included, with up to three original works per artist — no prints or mass-produced work — and a minimum age of 18. The juror is Silvana Foti, previously executive director of the David McCune International Art Gallery at Methodist University, where she was instrumental in the gallery's opening and the founding of its advisory board. She holds an MFA in printmaking and ceramic sculpture from the Art Institute of Chicago and the University of Notre Dame and a BFA from St Mary's College, and has curated regional, national and international exhibitions including Warhol, Chagall, The Story of the Exodus; Picasso: 25 Years of Edition Ceramics; Rodin: Portraits of a Lifetime; and Impressionism to Modernism: Masterworks of Early Photography, all meeting American Alliance of Museums standards. She taught at college level for more than twenty years and chaired Methodist University's Department of Art. Awards are First Place $450, Second $200, Third $100 and two Honorable Mentions of $50 each. Entries close 10 August 2026 through CaFÉ and the exhibition runs 25 September to 24 November 2026 in the main gallery. — Deadline: August 10, 2026. Fee: $30 + $15/additional entry. Prize: $450 / $200 / $100 + Exhibition.

item.title: Le Salon des Artistes 2026: Represent Your Culture · Denison Arts Council
item.description: The Denison Arts Council's second annual Salon des Artistes, a juried show in downtown Denison, Texas modelled on the historic Salon de Paris that began in 1667 — the original platform where creative expression, public support and institutional recognition met, and which shaped European art for centuries. This year's theme, inspired by the council's annual Día de los Muertos festival, is 'represent your culture': artists are asked to show how they connect with the people and places they descend from, through beloved recipes, cultural dress, family traditions or anything else that celebrates where they come from. The theme is open to interpretation and every work is considered with nuance, all media judged equally for prizes without regard to category — photography included. The juror is Jose Vargas, an independent exhibition curator and visual artist known for his work with the arts across the Dallas–Fort Worth metroplex and founder of the El Corazón and La Virgen de Guadalupe exhibitions in Dallas. The council advertises awards totalling $1,500, itemised in the prospectus as Best in Show $600, Second Place $400, Third Place $250, an Honorable Mention of $100 and a People's Choice of $100 decided by open voting from all guests and announced at the close of the show. Applications close 13 August 2026, electronic acceptance notifications go out 21 August, accepted work is dropped off in Denison on 6 September, and the exhibition opens to the public with an artists' night reception and award presentation on 12 September, with a midway reception on 10 October and a close on 7 November 2026. Note that the council cannot receive or return artwork by mail: accepted artists must arrange drop-off in person and collect work on 8 November. Photography is explicitly listed among the accepted media, wired and ready to hang, and the council retains 20% commission on works sold during the show. — Deadline: August 13, 2026. Fee: $40. Prize: $600 / $400 / $250 + Exhibition.

item.title: 30x30 2026 · Blue Line Arts
item.description: Blue Line Arts' annual challenge asks selected artists to make thirty original artworks in thirty days — a deliberate push to refine a practice, test an unfamiliar direction or simply work faster than deliberation allows. Every finished piece must measure precisely 6 by 6 inches, must hang securely on the wall (no pedestals, and no command strips or temporary hardware for 3D work), and 3D work may not extend more than 6 inches from the wall. Applicants do not submit the thirty pieces up front: the application takes 3–10 samples of existing work reflecting the direction intended for the challenge, and the gallery explicitly asks artists not to make the thirty artworks before being notified. Open to artists everywhere aged 18 and over, in any medium including photography; work must be original, completed within the last two years and never previously exhibited at Blue Line Arts. All pieces must be individually for sale, with the gallery handling sales — non-members receive 50% of gallery sales and members 60%. Entry is free for current Blue Line Arts Artist Members at the $75 level or above with a discount code from the gallery coordinator, and $25 for non-members covering 3 to 10 images. Applications close 4 September 2026 at 5pm Pacific, notifications go out 18 September, and the exhibition runs 24 November to 19 December 2026 in Roseville, with a reception on 19 December. — Deadline: September 4, 2026. Fee: $25 (free for members). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: LatinXperiencia 2026: La Resiliencia · Cabrillo Gallery
item.description: Cabrillo Gallery's annual LatinXperiencia series returns for National Hispanic Heritage Month with a call to Latino/a/x artists living anywhere in the US, working in any art media or discipline. The theme is resilience — the capacity that lets us bend without breaking, whether through personal upheaval such as illness, the end of a relationship or the death of someone we love, or through the larger pressures of authoritarianism, threats to immigrant communities and communities of colour, economic crisis, war and environmental disaster. Work does not have to address Latino/a/x themes or culture, though it can; the gallery welcomes any interpretation, imagery or content that captures the idea of resilience. Juried by Alyssarhaye Graciano, Visual Arts Curator at MACLA (Movimiento de Arte y Cultura Latino Americana) in San Jose, an author, textile artist and advocate for emerging and established artists of colour. Up to three works per artist; entries must be original and not previously shown at Cabrillo Gallery, and no AI-generated images will be considered. Three Juror's Awards of $300, $250 and $200 are presented. This is a physical exhibition — accepted artists deliver or ship work at their own expense and must include a prepaid return label. Selected artists are notified by 17 August. The show runs 28 September to 27 October 2026 at the gallery in Library 1002 on the Aptos campus, with a reception on 26 September and a curator's talk during it. The submission deadline was extended to 4 August. — Deadline: August 4, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: $300 / $250 / $200 + Exhibition.

item.title: New Works 2026 · Floyd Center for the Arts
item.description: A juried exhibition in the Hayloft Gallery at the Floyd Center for the Arts, built around the bold directions, fresh perspectives and evolving techniques of artists working in the Blue Ridge region. The show is looking for the new media, methods and creative journeys artists are embracing — experiments with unfamiliar materials, innovative processes, or fresh interpretations of traditional forms — and restricts entries to work made in the past two years, so it reads as a snapshot of where a practice is right now rather than a survey. All visual media are welcome, including photography; video entries must arrive with both the file and the display equipment plus installation directions, and artists of 3D work supply their own display. Open to artists 18 and over living within a 150-mile radius of the centre in Floyd, Virginia. Up to three works per artist. First ($200), Second ($150) and Third ($100) Place awards are presented along with a People's Choice ($50); the centre retains a 40% commission on sales, with 60% paid to the artist. The juror is being finalised and will be announced. Jurying runs 29 August to 6 September, notifications 8 September, delivery 8–16 September, and the exhibition opens 3 October with a reception 4–6pm, closing 21 November 2026. — Deadline: August 28, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: Cash awards + Exhibition.

item.title: Séance · Memento Mori Gallery & Tattoo
item.description: A haunted group show at Memento Mori, a lowbrow/outsider contemporary gallery and tattoo studio anchored in Lakewood's 40West Arts District, on the First Friday art-walk circuit and in the same shopping centre as Casa Bonita. Séance takes on communication beyond the veil — rituals, hauntings, folklore, spiritualism and the mysteries that linger between life and death — and the gallery asks for work that evokes tension, curiosity and the uncanny: shadow and silence, echoes and apparitions, the beauty and terror of what we cannot fully understand. Open nationally to 2D and 3D work; photographic work is welcome but must be printed and framed or mounted, ready to hang on a hook or nail, and the gallery will not accept photographs of another artist's artwork, street art included, without permission. Up to two pieces at $25 each. All work must be for sale with 40% of the sale going to the gallery, and out-of-state artists cover shipping both ways. Drop-off 29 August, show 4–25 September 2026, First Friday reception 4 September. — Deadline: August 8, 2026. Fee: $25 per piece. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Skull & Bones V · Memento Mori Gallery & Tattoo
item.description: The fifth edition of Memento Mori's annual group show for all things skeletal. The gallery is a lowbrow/outsider contemporary space and tattoo studio in Lakewood's 40West Arts District, on the First Friday art-walk circuit. Open nationally to 2D and 3D work; photographic work is welcome but must be printed and framed or mounted and arrive ready to hang from a hook or nail, and the gallery will not accept photographs depicting another artist's work, street art included, without permission. Up to two pieces at $30 each. All work must be for sale with 40% of the sale going to the gallery, and out-of-state artists are responsible for shipping in both directions. Drop-off 26 September, show 2–24 October 2026, First Friday reception 2 October. — Deadline: September 5, 2026. Fee: $30 per piece. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Krampusnacht IX · Memento Mori Gallery & Tattoo
item.description: Memento Mori's ninth annual Krampusnacht, a group exhibition celebrating the folklore, mystery and mischievous spirit of Krampus — from traditional Alpine legend to contemporary reinterpretation, and the eerie, playful, macabre and beautifully bizarre sides of the figure. The gallery is a lowbrow/outsider contemporary space and tattoo studio in Lakewood's 40West Arts District, on the First Friday art-walk circuit. Open nationally to 2D and 3D work; photographic work is welcome but must be printed and framed or mounted and ready to hang, and the gallery will not accept photographs depicting another artist's work, street art included, without permission. Up to two pieces at $25 each. All work must be for sale with 40% of the sale going to the gallery, and out-of-state artists cover shipping both ways. Drop-off 28 November, show 4–23 December 2026, First Friday reception 4 December. — Deadline: November 7, 2026. Fee: $25 per piece. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: The Modern Portrait · Site:Brooklyn Gallery
item.description: A new online juried exhibition from Site:Brooklyn tracing portraiture from cave painting through Holbein's construction of the sitter, Picabia's deconstruction of the body, Klee's abstractions and into the photographic worlds of Man Ray and August Sander. The gallery is looking for contemporary work that engages the portrait as subject or concept, material or metaphor — what the best portraiture attains, it argues, is a fusion of inner life and outer world. Juried by Theadora Walsh, whose writing and criticism have appeared in the Los Angeles Review of Books, Artforum, BOMB, Art Papers and SFMOMA's Open Space, and who runs the San Francisco curatorial project In Concert with Gabriel Garza. Open internationally to artists 18 and over working in all media. Submit 3–12 images; all work must be priced for sale and remain available for the run, with artists retaining a 60% commission. Exhibition online 2 October – 2 November 2026. — Deadline: September 9, 2026. Fee: $26 (3 images) + $10 each additional. Prize: Online exhibition.

item.title: I'M SCARED 2026 · Bethany Arts Community
item.description: The third edition of Bethany Arts Community's I'M SCARED series, born out of the questions of what it truly means to be scared, what shadows haunt your thoughts and what we should genuinely fear — and how you make space to show frightening work at all. The team describes what it wants through a list of guiding words: shadow, sorcery, dystopian, witchcraft, haunting, doom, nightmare, foreboding, grotesque, phantom, morbid curiosities, oddities. 2D work, 3D and sculpture, music and soundscapes, and film under five minutes are all accepted, so photographs and lens-based work sit squarely within scope. There is no entry fee. Artists must be 18 or over and able to hand-deliver and collect work themselves at the Ossining campus; 2D work must be wired for a STAS hook system, and the arts centre takes a 20% commission on sales. Notifications 4 September, drop-off 30 September and 1 October, gallery 10 October – 6 November 2026 with an opening reception on 10 October and a curator walk and talk on 21 October. — Deadline: August 13, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Mystery, Magic & the Macabre · Deines Cultural Center
item.description: A juried exhibition at the Deines Cultural Center in Russell, Kansas — a three-gallery centre built around the wood engravings of Prairie Printmaker E. Hubert Deines — looking for artists who bring thoughtfulness and unique insight to the magical, mystical and macabre. Photography is named explicitly among the accepted media alongside painting, sculpture and mixed media; installation, video and AI-generated work are excluded, as are copies, kits and giclée reproductions, and work depicting graphic violence will not be accepted. Entries must be original, made in the last three years, and not previously exhibited. Open to artists 18 and over living in the United States, up to three works at a $25 entry fee. Juried by David Barnes, retired director of the Shafer Gallery at Barton County Community College in Great Bend. Awards are $500 for first place, $250 for second and $150 for third, judged in person and announced at the 23 October reception. Notification 19 September, delivery by 7 October, exhibition 16 October – 20 November 2026. — Deadline: September 10, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: $500 + Exhibition.

item.title: SHIFT · NKollectiv
item.description: An open call for Colorado artists from NKollectiv, a curated gallery running since 2021 as the anchor of EASEL, the art hub in downtown Englewood. SHIFT invites work about what it feels like when something changes — a turning point, a quiet realisation, a spark of insight, or a collective moment that moves a whole community; the change of a season, of a belief, or the change inside us as we grow into a new version of ourselves. Photography is named explicitly among the welcome media alongside painting, sculpture, installation, mixed media and digital formats. Up to three works with an artist statement of 1,000 characters or less; 2D work must arrive ready to hang with D-rings and wire, no sawtooth hangers, and be delivered in person during the scheduled drop-off. Juried by Liz Graham of Liz Graham Art Consulting, with awards presented at the reception.
